- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 7–14 days.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +10% above recent mean), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use 3-period moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is trending up, model frequently overreacts; apply downward bias of 2–5% to avoid overconfidence in momentum.
- When true price drops sharply after a forecast peak, model often fails to adjust; use 2-period lagged true value as anchor for next 5–7 days.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.2–0.8) and price is near mean, model overfits short-term noise; use 10-day rolling mean as baseline for correction.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overpredicts early in the window; apply 3–5% downward adjustment for first 10 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment is 0.0–0.2 and price is falling, model often ignores trend; add 1–3% upward bias to avoid underestimating rebound potential.
